text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Peace pact brokered in troubled oil city of Warri breaks down 24 hours later as armed youths of rival Ijaw and Itsekiri tribes clash again killing at least two people.
- Kano state government cancels public holiday declared for Friday to enable residents welcome Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi when he arrives there later in the day on a one-day visit.
- Appeal court nullifies lower court order that state-run oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation should insure its properties with state insurer NICON.
- About 2,000 pump stations nationwide are to be closed down for failing to comply with registration requirements.
- Three oil firms led by Elf Petroleum Nigeria Limited have launched a new search for crude oil in Nigeria's deep offshore despite recent setbacks suffered in the area by some companies.
- Nigeria's foreign debt stands at $28 billion, restates the director-general of the finance ministry Umaru Alkaleri at a conference in the northern city of Kaduna.
- Eleven detainees awaiting trial escape from Abeokuta prison in the southwest, seven months after a similar jail break there in which 47 convicts absconded.
- Franco-Nigerian trading conglomerate CFAO Nigeria Plc posts marginal profit of 260.6 million naira in 1996 compared to 260.2 million naira in 1995.

- National electoral commission may propose to postpone to June 1998 governorship elections scheduled for the last quarter of this year. The proposal will follow suggestions by the five political parties that the polls should be deferred to 1998 so that they can be held at the same time as a presidential election meant to restore democracy fully.
- Demand for foreign exchange at weekly auction still high at $109.5 million this week compared to $109.8 million last week.
